model.name: Concept / Term
model.purpose: Represent a stable, identified semantic concept as a unit of thought that is independent of any label, language or storage format, together with the designations, definitions, notes and usage descriptions that describe it, so that agents and systems can refer to the same meaning across languages, vocabularies and interfaces.
model.scope_statement: WM-KNW-006 models the concept as an aggregate root with its own persistent identity, plus the subordinate or referenced descriptions that give it meaning: designations (terms, appellations, proper names, symbols) with acceptability ratings, lexical entries and word forms, definitions and typed notes, subject field, referents and usage context; the concept's placement in concept schemes and its hierarchical, associative and cross-scheme mapping relations; and its lifecycle, provenance, ownership, editorial governance, access policy references and quality assertions. The model is format-neutral: RDF/SKOS, TBX, OntoLex, JSON, YAML, Markdown, Git, MCP and document stores are projections of the same semantics. External standards are treated as alignments, not as conformance claims.
in_scope: Concept identity: authoritative identifier, governed IRI, notation, and the rules that decide when a change breaks identity
Concept delimitation: intension, extension, essential and delimiting characteristics, split/merge and duplicate tests
Concept kind: general versus individual concept, and explicit separation from lexical entry, word form, sense, class/type, referent and free-text keyword
Designations attached to the concept: term, appellation, proper name and non-linguistic symbol, with preferred/admitted/deprecated acceptability ratings and hidden retrieval-only labels
Designation-level identity and attributes where terms are reified rather than carried as plain strings
Language, script, region and variant tagging of every designation, definition and note, plus transliteration and romanization
Lexical description at the designation boundary: lexical entry, canonical form, other forms, written and phonetic representation, grammatical categories
Definitions and typed notes: scope note, example, general note, editorial note, and their attachment level
Subject field assignment and homograph disambiguation across domains
Referents and exemplars denoted by the concept, held as references to external entity records
Usage context: audience, register, territory, discouraged usage and attested occurrences
Multilingual equivalence asserted at the designation and sense boundary
Concept scheme membership, top-concept status and scheme-scoped constraints
Hierarchical, associative and instantial semantic relations between concepts
Cross-scheme concept mappings and their degree of match
Concept and designation lifecycle: status, supersession, deprecation, redirect and versioning
Provenance, ownership, editorial authority and change history
Access-policy references, quality assertions and validation profiles for concept records
out_of_scope: The real-world objects and entity records that a concept denotes; their attributes, identity resolution and lifecycle belong to domain entity models
Formal ontology axiomatisation and reasoning: OWL/RDFS class semantics, restrictions, entailment and consistency checking
Publication of a full lexical or lexicographic resource (dictionary entries, sense inventories, corpora, annotation layers) beyond the designation-level description carried here
Documents, records and content items that merely mention or are indexed with a concept
Search, retrieval, ranking and indexing engines that consume designations
Translation-management workflow, translation memory segments and localisation project state
Identifier minting and resolution infrastructure such as PID, handle or DOI services
Runtime access-control evaluation, policy enforcement and audit-trail storage; this model carries policy and audit-record references only
Machine-learning embeddings, vector representations and similarity models derived from concepts
Retention scheduling, legal hold and physical destruction execution, which belong to the adopting Dimension's records policy

boundary_notes.neighbor: Lexical entry and word form (OntoLex-Lemon lexicon)
boundary_notes.distinction: A lexical entry is a unit of the lexicon with grammatically related forms and base meanings; a concept is a unit of thought. This model attaches lexical entries and forms at the designation boundary and references the lexicon, but does not own the lexicon's entry inventory or its editorial lifecycle.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Class or type in a formal ontology
boundary_notes.distinction: SKOS concepts are individuals of skos:Concept, not classes; the SKOS Primer records that OWL DL forbids treating them as classes. A concept record may be aligned with an owl:Class under a documented punning rule, but class axioms, restrictions and entailment stay in the ontology model.

ISO 1087 separates the object (anything perceivable or conceivable) from the concept (a mental unit combining characteristics of objects). This model records which referents a concept denotes as references; the referent's own master data belongs elsewhere.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Concept scheme, thesaurus or controlled vocabulary (parent WM-KNW-002)
boundary_notes.distinction: The scheme owns membership, top-concept designation, scheme versioning and scheme-wide editorial policy. A concept carries an inScheme reference; the same concept may participate in more than one scheme without the scheme's rules migrating into the concept record.

A keyword is an uncontrolled string with no identity, no rating, no language governance and no definition. A designation in this model is always bound to an identified concept and carries a language tag and an acceptability rating.

A sense pairs one lexical entry with one reference; equivalence asserted sense-to-sense is narrower than equivalence asserted concept-to-concept. This model records which level an equivalence claim was made at, but does not maintain a sense inventory.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Notation, code list and classification registry
boundary_notes.distinction: skos:notation is a lexical code unique within a concept scheme, typed by datatype. The code list itself, its allocation rules and its release cycle are owned by the issuing registry, not by the concept record that cites the code.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Semantic relations, mappings, lifecycle, provenance, access and quality areas of WM-KNW-006
boundary_notes.distinction: These are in scope for the combined model but are specified in separate areas. The semantic core carries only the identity-breaking trigger that forces a split or merge, reference-only pointers to rating authority and definition source, and no relation, status, approval or audit machinery of its own.

sources.title: SKOS Simple Knowledge Organization System Reference
sources.relevance: Normative definitions of skos:Concept, prefLabel/altLabel/hiddenLabel with integrity conditions S13 (pairwise disjoint) and S14 (at most one prefLabel per language tag), skos:notation (S15), and the documentation note properties definition, scopeNote, example, note, editorialNote, historyNote and changeNote.

sources.title: SKOS Simple Knowledge Organization System eXtension for Labels (SKOS-XL), section of the SKOS Reference
sources.relevance: Basis for treating a designation as an identified resource: skosxl:Label with exactly one skosxl:literalForm, skosxl:prefLabel/altLabel/hiddenLabel, and skosxl:labelRelation for relations between labels.

sources.title: SKOS Simple Knowledge Organization System Primer
sources.relevance: Guidance that concepts are units of thought distinct from the resources they denote, that SKOS concepts are OWL individuals rather than classes in OWL DL, the one-preferred-label-per-language-tag rule, notation styles, note typing, and the requirement to use BCP 47 language tags.

sources.title: Lexicon Model for Ontologies: Community Report
sources.relevance: Defines LexicalEntry, Word, MultiwordExpression, Affix, Form with canonicalForm/otherForm/writtenRep/phoneticRep, LexicalSense, LexicalConcept as a subclass of skos:Concept, and the denotes/reference/sense/evokes properties that fix the concept-designation-sense-referent boundary.

sources.title: MVF ISO 1087 Vocabulary for Terms and Definitions (RDF)
sources.version_or_date: OMG-published RDF rendering accompanying MVF 1.1, retrieved 2026-09-02
sources.relevance: Publicly retrievable rendering of the ISO 1087 vocabulary: object, concept, designation, term, appellation, symbol, proper name, definition, essential and delimiting characteristic, preferred/admitted/deprecated term, subject field and concept system. Used as the evidence route for ISO 1087 notions because the standard's clause text is paywalled.

sources.title: Multiple Vocabulary Facility (MVF) specification page
sources.relevance: Specification for expressing one model element through multiple natural languages and terminologies, with normative mappings to ISO 1087 and SKOS; supports the separation of concept entry, vocabulary and designation and the machine-readable RDF/TTL delivery of terminology.

sources.title: ISO 25964 — the international standard for thesauri and interoperability with other vocabularies
sources.version_or_date: Part 1 published 2011, Part 2 published 2013; SKOS correspondence published 11 December 2013
sources.relevance: Maintenance page for the ISO 25964 data model, its XML schema and the published correspondence between ISO 25964, SKOS, SKOS-XL and MADS; establishes the reified thesaurus-term view of designations and the preferred/non-preferred distinction.

sources.title: SKOS-Thes: ISO 25964 SKOS extension namespace documentation
sources.organization: Dublin Core Metadata Initiative (hosting the ISO 25964 SKOS extension by A. Isaac and J. De Smedt)
sources.relevance: Machine-readable classes PreferredTerm, SimpleNonPreferredTerm, SplitNonPreferredTerm, CompoundEquivalence, ConceptGroup and ThesaurusArray, and the status data property applying to concepts or labels; documents that custom term and concept attributes remain unmodelled.

sources.title: RFC 5646: Tags for Identifying Languages (BCP 47)
sources.relevance: Normative subtag order (language, extlang, script, region, variant, extension, private use), the IANA Language Subtag Registry with Deprecated, Preferred-Value, Prefix and Suppress-Script fields, and the guidance not to state a script subtag that is suppressed for the language.

sources.title: ISO 15924 Registration Authority — Codes for the representation of names of scripts
sources.version_or_date: ISO 15924:2022; code list maintained and distributed by the Registration Authority, retrieved 2026-09-02
sources.relevance: Authoritative source of four-letter script codes and their maintenance process; supplies the value space for the script subtag used on designations, definitions and notes.

sources.title: RFC 3339: Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps
sources.relevance: Defines full-date, full-time and the mandatory seconds field plus the time-offset as Z or +/-hh:mm, and notes that -00:00 differs semantically from Z; used for the model's timestamp rule.

sources.title: Introduction to TermBase eXchange (TBX)
sources.organization: TBX Info (complement to ISO 30042, maintained with LTAC Global)
sources.version_or_date: TBX Version 3 published 2019 as ISO 30042:2019; site retrieved 2026-09-02
sources.relevance: First-party description of concept-oriented terminological interchange, the TBX-Core, TBX-Min and TBX-Basic dialects and modules, and the publicly available RNG, XSD and Schematron validation artefacts; grounds the interchange-profile and loss-report functions.

sources.title: ISO 1087:2019 Terminology work and terminology science — Vocabulary
sources.relevance: Catalogue entry cited as the origin of the terminology-science vocabulary used here. Automated retrieval of this page returned HTTP 403 and the clause text is paywalled, so no clause is quoted or relied upon directly; every ISO 1087 notion used in this model is evidenced through the publicly retrievable OMG rendering SRC-005.

bundles.name: Concept identity and delimitation
bundles.description: What makes this concept a single, citable unit of thought: how it is identified, what fixes its boundaries against neighbouring concepts, what kind of concept it is, and which real-world referents it denotes.
bundles.rationale: ISO 1087 and SKOS both treat the concept, not the label, as the unit that carries identity; SKOS notation is scheme-scoped and labels are language-scoped, so neither can serve as the identifier. Delimitation by essential and delimiting characteristics is the only defensible test for whether two records are the same concept.

layers.name: Identity and delimitation
layers.description: Identifier assignment and the intensional and extensional criteria that fix the concept's boundary and drive split, merge and duplicate decisions.

findings.name: Concept identifier and identity basis
findings.description: The concept holds a persistent identifier independent of any label, definition wording, language or scheme. Records the assigning master system, an optional governed IRI, scheme-scoped notations, and the rule set that separates identity-preserving edits from identity-breaking changes.

questions.text: Which authoritative master system assigns this concept's primary identifier, and what is that identifier value?
Does the concept have a governed IRI, and which body controls the namespace it is minted in?
Which notations or classification codes denote this concept, and in which coding scheme is each one valid?
answer_data: Scope of validity for the notation

questions.text: Which changes preserve the identifier, and which force a new concept identifier rather than an edit?
answer_data: Reference to the split or merge rule that applies

data_elements.name: Concept primary identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier assigned by the authoritative master system for the concept; never derived from a label, notation or date.

data_elements.name: Governed concept IRI
data_elements.description: Dereferenceable IRI in a namespace controlled by a named authority, used for linked-data projections.

data_elements.name: Notation
data_elements.description: Typed lexical code that denotes the concept within a stated coding scheme; unique within that scheme only.

data_elements.name: Identity rule reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the documented rule set that decides identity-breaking versus identity-preserving change for this vocabulary.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Identity is pure reference data. Identifiers, namespaces and notations are literal values that every projection must carry inline; no media-bearing or form-bearing artifact would add meaning, and binding identity to a file would make the identifier depend on a storage format the model is explicitly independent of.

findings.name: Intension, extension and delimiting characteristics
findings.description: The characteristics an object must have to fall under the concept, how far the extension reaches, and which characteristic distinguishes the concept from its nearest confusable neighbour. Supplies the operational test for duplicate detection and for split and merge decisions.

questions.text: Which essential characteristics must an object have for it to fall under this concept?
answer_data: Whether each characteristic is asserted locally or taken from a source standard

questions.text: Which delimiting characteristic separates this concept from the nearest concept it is confused with?
How is the extension bounded — open, enumerated or sampled by exemplars?
What evidence supports this delimitation — attested usage, expert ruling or a cited source clause?
When two records share designations, which test decides whether they are one concept or two?
answer_data: Deciding characteristic that carried the outcome

data_elements.name: Characteristic
data_elements.description: A single characteristic asserted of the concept, typed as essential or non-essential.

data_elements.name: Delimiting characteristic
data_elements.description: Essential characteristic used to distinguish this concept from a stated related concept.

data_elements.name: Extension boundedness
data_elements.description: Code stating whether the concept's extension is open, enumerated or exemplar-sampled.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Characteristics and delimitation statements are short structured assertions consumed by reasoning and duplicate-detection logic. Externalising them as artifacts would hide the very data the split or merge decision depends on and would prevent constraint evaluation over the record itself.

layers.name: Concept kind and referents
layers.description: Typing the record against its neighbours and recording which real-world objects it denotes, without absorbing those objects' own master data.

findings.name: Concept kind and neighbour typing
findings.description: Classifies the record as a general concept covering many objects or an individual concept covering exactly one, and asserts explicitly what it is not: not a lexical entry, not a word form, not a sense, not an OWL or RDFS class, not the referent, and not a free-text keyword. Prevents category errors during projection.

questions.text: Is this a general concept covering many objects, or an individual concept covering exactly one?
answer_data: Whether a proper name designates it

questions.text: When projected into a formal ontology, is this an individual of skos:Concept, an owl:Class, or both under a documented punning rule?
answer_data: OWL flavour assumed (OWL Full or OWL DL)
Reference to the punning rule if both are asserted

questions.text: Which neighbouring construct — lexical entry, word form, sense, referent, class or keyword — has previously been conflated with this record?
answer_data: Where the conflation occurred (system or profile)

questions.text: What distinguishes this concept record from an uncontrolled keyword or tag carrying the same string?

data_elements.name: Concept kind
data_elements.description: Code distinguishing a general concept from an individual concept.

data_elements.name: Ontology projection typing
data_elements.description: Declared typing used when the concept is projected into RDF or OWL, including the OWL flavour assumed.

data_elements.name: Negative typing assertion
data_elements.description: Explicit statement of a neighbouring construct that this record is not, retained to prevent recurring conflation.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Typing decisions are single-valued codes and short justifications that must be readable by validators before any projection is attempted; there is no media form in which they could sensibly be held.

findings.name: Referents, exemplars and denotation
findings.description: Which objects or entity records the concept denotes, and which exemplars illustrate it without being equated with it. Keeps the ISO 1087 object and concept split and the OntoLex reference and evokes split intact, holding referents as external references only.

questions.text: Which real-world objects or entity records does this concept denote, and in which model are those referents mastered?
answer_data: Denotation basis (extension membership or individual identity)

questions.text: Which exemplar, type specimen or illustration is used to show the concept without being equated with it?
answer_data: Statement that the exemplar is not the concept

questions.text: Does any designation denote the referent directly rather than through the concept, and how is that recorded?
answer_data: Target ontology entity or sense reference

questions.text: What is explicitly not a referent of this concept despite being commonly assumed to be one?
answer_data: Concept that does cover it, where known

data_elements.name: Referent reference
data_elements.description: Reference to an externally mastered object or entity record denoted by the concept.

data_elements.name: Exemplar role
data_elements.description: Role played by an exemplar: typical instance, boundary case or explicit counterexample.

artifacts.name: Referent exemplar record
artifacts.description: Media or specimen record used to illustrate what falls under the concept, held separately from the concept so the illustration is never mistaken for the unit of thought.
artifacts.identity_strategy: The asset identifier assigned by the holding system takes priority; where none exists, a content hash of the exemplar file is used. The exemplar is linked to the concept identifier and never carries or substitutes for it.

bundles.name: Designations and linguistic form
bundles.description: The signs that represent the concept — terms, appellations, proper names and symbols — with their acceptability ratings, their own identity where needed, their language and script tagging, their lexical description, and cross-language equivalence at the designation boundary.
bundles.rationale: ISO 1087 treats designation as a construct distinct from concept, and SKOS constrains labels (at most one preferred label per language tag, pairwise disjoint label properties). SKOS-XL and ISO 25964 reify terms so that ratings, sources and grammatical data can attach to the designation rather than the concept; OntoLex supplies the lexical description layer.

layers.name: Designation inventory and identity
layers.description: Which signs represent the concept, how they are rated and typed, and when a designation must become an identified object in its own right.

findings.name: Designation inventory and acceptability rating
findings.description: The set of designations attached to the concept, each typed as term, appellation, proper name or non-linguistic symbol, each rated preferred, admitted or deprecated, and each marked as displayed or hidden for retrieval only. Carries the uniqueness constraint on preferred designations per language tag.

questions.text: Which designation is rated preferred in each language, and which are admitted, deprecated or hidden?
What designation type is each sign — term, appellation, proper name or non-linguistic symbol?
answer_data: Justification where the type is contested
Whether a lexical entry exists for it

questions.text: Which rating-authority reference is carried on the designation, given that the rating process itself is governed outside this area?
answer_data: Pointer to the governing process record

questions.text: Can two designations share the same rating in one language, and which constraint prevents duplicate preferred labels?
answer_data: Profile decision where the constraint is relaxed

questions.text: Which non-linguistic symbol represents the concept, and in what medium is that symbol fixed?

data_elements.name: Designation literal form
data_elements.description: The written form of a linguistic designation, always carried with a language tag.

data_elements.name: Designation type
data_elements.description: Code distinguishing term, appellation, proper name and symbol.

data_elements.name: Acceptability rating
data_elements.description: Rating of the designation as preferred, admitted or deprecated on a named scale.

data_elements.name: Hidden designation flag
data_elements.description: Marks a designation as available to text-based retrieval but suppressed from display, for example a known misspelling.

artifacts.name: Non-linguistic symbol asset
artifacts.description: Graphical or glyph asset that designates the concept by non-linguistic means, such as a hazard pictogram, unit symbol or standardised graphical symbol.
artifacts.identity_strategy: The symbol identifier issued by the standardising authority takes priority; otherwise a content hash bound to the designation record identifier. The symbol asset never carries the concept identifier by itself.

findings.name: Designation as an identified object
findings.description: When a designation must carry its own attributes — rating history, defining source, grammatical data, relations to other designations — it is reified as an identified object rather than held as a plain string. Covers the SKOS-XL Label, the ISO 25964 preferred and non-preferred term classes and the TBX term section, and the constraint that a reified label has exactly one literal form.

questions.text: Does this designation carry its own identifier, and which system assigns it?
answer_data: Whether reification is required by the active profile

questions.text: Which attributes are held on the designation rather than on the concept, and why does each belong there?
answer_data: Attribute names held at designation level
Attributes deliberately kept at concept level

questions.text: How is a plain-string projection kept consistent with the reified designation's single literal form?
Which relations hold between designations of the same concept, such as abbreviation of, variant of or transliteration of?

data_elements.name: Designation identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of a reified designation, enabling attributes and relations to attach to the sign itself.

data_elements.name: Designation-to-designation relation
data_elements.description: Typed relation between two designations of the same concept, such as abbreviation or transliteration.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Reified designations are structured records of identifiers, codes and short literals evaluated by constraint checks; they are not media. Holding them as artifacts would break the exactly-one-literal-form constraint that has to be checkable in the record itself.

layers.name: Language, script and lexical form
layers.description: How every designation, definition and note is language-tagged and scripted, and how the linguistic description of a designation is recorded without leaking into the concept.

findings.name: Language tag, script, region and transliteration
findings.description: Every language-bearing value carries a BCP 47 tag built in the normative subtag order; the script subtag is taken from ISO 15924 and stated only when it is not suppressed for the language. Covers region and variant subtags, transliteration and romanization provenance, and language fallback behaviour.

questions.text: Which complete BCP 47 language tag applies to this designation, including script, region and variant subtags where they are meaningful?
answer_data: Script, region and variant subtags used

questions.text: Is the script subtag suppressed for this language, and if it is present anyway, what justifies including it?
answer_data: Suppress-Script value from the subtag registry

questions.text: Which transliteration or romanization scheme produced this designation, and what is its source designation?
Where a designation is region-specific, which territory or usage community does it apply to?
answer_data: Region subtag or UN M.49 code
Territories where the designation is not current

questions.text: How should a consuming system behave when no designation exists for the requested language tag?
answer_data: Whether an untagged or notation value may be returned

data_elements.name: Language tag
data_elements.description: BCP 47 tag applied to a designation, definition or note; validated against the IANA Language Subtag Registry.

data_elements.name: Script code
data_elements.description: ISO 15924 four-letter script code, recorded only where it is not suppressed for the language.

data_elements.name: Transliteration scheme reference
data_elements.description: Identifier of the romanization or transliteration scheme that produced a derived designation.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Language, script and region values are registry-controlled codes that must travel with every literal in every projection. They are validated against external registries by reference, so no artifact is created or stored by this model.

findings.name: Lexical entry, word forms and grammatical description
findings.description: The linguistic description subordinate to a designation: the lexical entry realising it (word, multiword expression or affix), its canonical form, other forms, written and phonetic representations and grammatical categories. Attached at the designation boundary because symbols and appellations may have no lexical entry at all.

questions.text: Which lexical entry realises this designation, and is it a single word, a multiword expression or an affix?
answer_data: Lexicon or lexical resource that masters the entry

questions.text: What is the canonical form of the designation, and which other forms are recorded alongside it?
Which grammatical categories are asserted, and from which data-category registry are their values drawn?
answer_data: Part of speech value and registry reference

questions.text: What evidence fixes the pronunciation or spoken form of this designation?
Which forms must not be treated as separate designations of the concept?
answer_data: Forms excluded from the designation inventory

data_elements.name: Canonical form
data_elements.description: The lemma or citation form of the lexical entry realising a designation.

data_elements.name: Other form
data_elements.description: A non-canonical grammatical realisation of the lexical entry, with its written representation.

data_elements.name: Grammatical category value
data_elements.description: Part of speech, gender, number or similar category value drawn from a named data-category registry.

data_elements.name: Phonetic representation
data_elements.description: Phonetic transcription of a form, with the transcription notation named.

artifacts.name: Pronunciation record
artifacts.description: Spoken realisation of a designation captured as audio or as a formal phonetic transcription document, used where the written form underdetermines pronunciation.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identifier assigned by the holding lexical or media system where one exists; otherwise a content hash bound to the designation identifier and the recorded language tag.

layers.name: Cross-language equivalence
layers.description: How designations in different languages are asserted to represent the same concept, and how gaps and partial equivalence are recorded.

findings.name: Multilingual equivalence at the designation and sense boundary
findings.description: Assertions that designations in different languages represent this one concept, with the degree of equivalence, the level at which the claim was made (concept-to-concept or sense-to-sense), the evidence behind it, and the way a missing target-language designation is recorded without inventing a term. Concept-to-concept mapping across schemes is deliberately excluded.

questions.text: Which designations in other languages are asserted to represent this same concept, and at what degree of equivalence?
Where a target language has no designation, how is that gap recorded without coining a term?
answer_data: Descriptive gloss provided instead of a term
Whether coinage is permitted and by whom

questions.text: Is equivalence asserted concept-to-concept or sense-to-sense, and what follows for downstream reuse?
answer_data: Reference to the sense records where sense-level

questions.text: What evidence supports each equivalence assertion?
answer_data: Evidence type (parallel text, expert attestation, standard clause)
Date of attestation in RFC 3339 form

questions.text: Which equivalence claims are known to be partial or contested, and how is that flagged?

data_elements.name: Degree of equivalence
data_elements.description: Code stating whether a cross-language designation is exact, close, partial or a descriptive gloss.

data_elements.name: Equivalence assertion level
data_elements.description: Whether the equivalence was asserted at concept level or at sense level.

data_elements.name: No-equivalent marker
data_elements.description: Explicit marker recording that a language has no designation for the concept, distinguished from missing data.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Equivalence claims are assertions between records already held in this model, plus a small set of qualifiers. Their supporting documents are cited by reference to sources owned by the provenance area, so this finding declares no artifact of its own.

bundles.name: Definition, scope and usage
bundles.description: The written descriptions that make the concept understandable and usable: definitions, typed notes, subject field and homograph disambiguation, and the usage context and attestation of its designations.
bundles.rationale: ISO 1087 defines a definition as a representation of the concept that describes it and differentiates it from related concepts; SKOS supplies the typed note vocabulary and requires language tagging. Subject field is the standard disambiguator for homographic terms, and attested usage is the evidence base for acceptability ratings.

layers.name: Definitions and notes
layers.description: The intensional statement of meaning and the typed documentation attached around it.

findings.name: Definition of the concept
findings.description: The statement that describes the concept and differentiates it from related concepts, recorded per language with a definition type, the delimiting characteristic it carries, the source it is taken or adapted from, and checks against circular and purely negative definitions.

questions.text: What is the definition text in each language, and which language tag applies to each version?
answer_data: Whether the version is an original or a translation

questions.text: Is the definition intensional, extensional or ostensive, and which delimiting characteristic does it carry?
answer_data: Broader concept named in the definition, if any

questions.text: From which source document, clause or authority is the definition taken or adapted?
How many definitions may coexist per language, and which rule resolves competing definitions?
answer_data: Cardinality rule for definitions per language

questions.text: Which check confirms that the definition is neither circular nor a bare negation of another concept?
answer_data: Terms in the definition that resolve to other concepts

data_elements.name: Definition text
data_elements.description: Language-tagged statement describing the concept and differentiating it from related concepts.

data_elements.name: Definition type
data_elements.description: Code distinguishing intensional, extensional and ostensive definitions.

data_elements.name: Definition source reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the document, clause or authority the definition derives from; the provenance chain itself is owned elsewhere.

findings.inline_only_rationale: A definition is a short language-tagged literal that must appear in every projection and be diffable and constraint-checkable; storing it as an artifact would put the primary meaning-bearing value outside the record that validators and consumers read.

findings.name: Scope notes, examples and explanatory notes
findings.description: Typed documentation attached either to the concept or to a specific designation: scope note, example, general note and editorial note. Separates meaning-bearing notes that must survive interchange from editorial notes that may be filtered, and keeps change and history notes with the lifecycle and provenance areas.

questions.text: Which note types are recorded, and does each attach to the concept or to a specific designation?
What does the scope note state as included in and excluded from the concept's coverage?
Which examples illustrate correct and incorrect use of the designation?
answer_data: Reference to the designation the example applies to

questions.text: Which notes are meaning-bearing and must survive interchange, and which are editorial and may be filtered?
answer_data: Note type classification as meaning-bearing or editorial
Behaviour of each target interchange profile
Loss report entry where a note cannot be carried

data_elements.name: Note type
data_elements.description: Code identifying the note as a scope note, example, general note or editorial note.

data_elements.name: Note text
data_elements.description: Language-tagged documentation text attached to a concept or designation.

data_elements.name: Note attachment level
data_elements.description: Whether the note attaches to the concept or to a named designation.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Notes are short language-tagged literals whose type determines whether an interchange profile can carry them; the filtering decision has to be made over inline values, so externalising them as artifacts would defeat the loss reporting this finding exists to support.

layers.name: Subject field and usage
layers.description: The domain that bounds the concept and disambiguates homographs, and the audience, register, territory and attested usage of its designations.

findings.name: Subject field and homograph disambiguation
findings.description: The field of special knowledge in which the concept and its terms are valid, drawn from an external classification. Used to disambiguate homographic designations across domains and to bound the intension; the classification itself is referenced, never redefined here.

questions.text: Which subject field does this concept belong to, and from which classification is that value drawn?
answer_data: Whether the assignment is primary or secondary

questions.text: Which other concept shares a designation with this one in a different subject field, and how is the pair distinguished?
answer_data: Disambiguating qualifier applied to the designation

questions.text: Does the subject field change the concept's delimitation, or only the usage of its designations?
Which classification is authoritative for subject-field values, and what happens when it is revised?

data_elements.name: Subject field value
data_elements.description: Referenced value from an external subject-field or domain classification.

data_elements.name: Homograph qualifier
data_elements.description: Qualifier added to a designation to distinguish it from a homograph in another subject field.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Subject field is a referenced classification value plus a short qualifier; the classification is owned by an external registry, so this model holds only inline reference values and would gain nothing from an artifact.

findings.name: Usage context, register, audience and attestation
findings.description: How and by whom a designation is actually used: audience and register, territory of currency, discouraged or offensive usage with directed alternatives, and attested occurrences that evidence real use. Keeps a designation's usage status distinct from the concept's own status, which belongs to the lifecycle area.

questions.text: For which audience and register is this designation appropriate — specialist, general public, regulatory or internal?
answer_data: Restriction on use outside that audience

questions.text: Which attested occurrence evidences that the designation is really used in this sense?
In which territory or community is the designation current, and where is it not used?
answer_data: Territories where it is not used
Region subtag applied to the designation

questions.text: Which usage is flagged as discouraged or offensive, and which alternative is directed instead?
How is a designation's usage status kept distinct from the concept's own status?
answer_data: Usage status value at designation level
Statement that concept status is held in the lifecycle area
Rule preventing propagation between the two

data_elements.name: Audience and register
data_elements.description: Codes describing the intended audience and stylistic register for a designation.

data_elements.name: Usage territory
data_elements.description: Territory or community in which a designation is current, expressed with a region subtag or named community.

data_elements.name: Attestation event time
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 date-time at which the attested use occurred, recorded separately from when this model ingested the attestation.

data_elements.name: Discouraged usage flag
data_elements.description: Marks a designation as discouraged or offensive and points to the directed alternative.

artifacts.name: Usage attestation record
artifacts.description: Captured evidence that a designation is used for this concept in real text or speech: a source excerpt, concordance line, screenshot of published use or a citation record.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Attestations accumulate per designation as an ordered series; identity is the designation identifier plus the zero-padded series number assigned by the owning package, together with a content hash of the captured excerpt. No date component is used in the identifier.

functions.name: Establish a concept identity
functions.description: Create a new concept record with a persistent identifier and an initial delimitation, after confirming that no existing concept already covers the same intension.
inputs: Essential and delimiting characteristics proposed for the concept
Assigning master system or governed namespace
outputs: Concept record carrying a primary identifier
preconditions: A duplicate test has been run against existing concepts sharing any candidate designation
The authority controlling the identifier namespace is known and reachable
At least one delimiting characteristic distinguishes the new concept from its nearest neighbour
effects: A citable concept identifier exists and can be referenced by other models
No scheme membership, editorial status or approval is asserted; those remain with the scheme and lifecycle areas
The identity rule reference in force at creation is recorded for later split and merge decisions

functions.name: Attach a designation to a concept
functions.description: Attach a term, appellation, proper name or symbol to an existing concept with its language tag, designation type and acceptability rating, reifying the designation where the active profile requires designation-level attributes.
inputs: Designation literal form or symbol asset reference
BCP 47 language tag and optional script subtag
outputs: Designation record linked to the concept
Reified designation identifier where the profile requires one
Constraint evaluation result for preferred-label uniqueness
preconditions: The language tag validates against the IANA Language Subtag Registry and any script subtag is justified against Suppress-Script
No conflicting preferred designation already exists for the same language tag unless the profile documents a relaxation
effects: The designation inventory is updated and the uniqueness constraint is re-evaluated
The rating-authority pointer is stored as a reference only; the rating process, its approval and its audit record stay outside this model
Hidden designations become available to retrieval without becoming displayable

functions.name: Record a definition or typed note
functions.description: Attach a language-tagged definition or a typed note to a concept or to a specific designation, with its source reference and attachment level.
outputs: Typed definition or note attached at the declared level
Classification of the note as meaning-bearing or editorial
preconditions: The note type is drawn from the declared note vocabulary
The definition cardinality rule for the target language permits the addition
effects: The meaning description of the concept is extended
Editorial notes are marked filterable so interchange profiles can drop them without loss of meaning
Circularity and bare-negation checks are queued for the validation function

functions.name: Resolve a designation to candidate concepts
functions.description: Look up a string in a given language and optional subject field and return the concepts whose designations match, with the evidence needed to disambiguate homographs.
inputs: Language tag and optional fallback order
Whether hidden designations are in scope
outputs: Matched designation with its type, rating and language tag
Homograph disambiguation evidence including subject field and delimiting characteristic
preconditions: The caller is authorised to read the designations in scope under the adopting Dimension's policy
The language fallback order is declared
effects: Read-only: no concept, designation or note is modified
Hidden designations may be matched but are not returned for display unless the caller is explicitly permitted
A no-designation signal is returned rather than a coined term when no match exists in the requested language

functions.name: Validate a concept record against declared constraints
functions.description: Check a concept record and its designations, definitions and notes against the structural constraints declared for the active profile, and return findings.
inputs: Concept record with its designations, definitions and notes
Registry endpoints for language and script code validation
outputs: List of constraint findings with severity and constraint identifier
Statement of which constraints were not evaluated and why
preconditions: The applicable profile has been declared
Any referenced registry is reachable, or its unavailability is reported rather than assumed to pass
effects: Findings are returned to the caller only
No remediation, no enforcement and no audit record is written; enforcement and audit storage belong to the adopting Dimension and to the governance area
A failed constraint marks the record unverified rather than altering it

functions.name: Project a concept set to or from an interchange profile
functions.description: Render concepts and their designations into a named interchange profile, or read them back, producing an explicit report of anything the target profile cannot carry.
inputs: Target profile identifier such as SKOS, SKOS-XL with the ISO 25964 extension, TBX or OntoLex
outputs: Profile-shaped projection of the selected concepts
Loss report naming every attribute the target profile cannot represent
Mapping table used for the projection
preconditions: A documented mapping exists for the target profile
Where the profile reifies designations, designation identifiers exist for every designation in scope
effects: Model semantics are unchanged; the projection is a rendering, not a redefinition
A loss report is produced whenever designation-level attributes or note types cannot be carried
No conformance to the target standard is claimed unless validation evidence for that profile is attached

composition.target: WM-KNW-002 — concept scheme or knowledge organization system (registered parent)
composition.purpose: A concept is registered as a member of one or more schemes. This model carries only the inScheme reference and any scheme-scoped notation; scheme membership rules, top-concept designation, scheme versioning and scheme-wide editorial policy remain with the parent.

Express concept identity, labels, notation and typed notes in RDF, including reified labels where designation-level attributes are needed. Alignment only: conformance is claimed solely where a validated profile and evidence exist.

Attach lexical entries, canonical and other forms, written and phonetic representations and senses at the designation boundary. The lexicon's own entry inventory, sense inventory and editorial lifecycle remain in the lexical resource.

Map reified preferred and non-preferred terms and the term-level status property. The extension's hierarchical relation properties are used by the relations area of this model, not by the semantic core.

Support concept-oriented terminological interchange of designations, grammatical data and usage notes, and drive the loss report when a dialect cannot carry an attribute. Dialect validation artefacts remain with the TBX specification.

Supplies the value space and validity rules for language, extlang, region and variant subtags, including Deprecated, Preferred-Value and Suppress-Script handling. Registry maintenance, subtag deprecation and republication remain with IANA and the IETF.

composition.target: ISO 15924 script code registry (Unicode Consortium Registration Authority)
composition.purpose: Supplies four-letter script code values for the script subtag. Code allocation, change requests and distribution remain with the Registration Authority.

composition.target: Subject field or domain classification model
composition.purpose: Supplies subject-field values used to bound the concept and disambiguate homographs. Classification structure, maintenance and revision handling remain in that model; this model stores the referenced value and its classification version.

Identifies the objects the concept denotes. Entity attributes, identity resolution, matching and lifecycle remain in the entity model; this model records the denotation link and the exclusion statements.

Map a concept entry and its designation sets onto model elements expressed in multiple natural languages and terminologies, using MVF's normative mappings to ISO 1087 and SKOS. MVF's model-management semantics remain with MVF.

owner_package_requirements: The adopting Dimension names one owning package for concept identity and one for each language community that maintains designations, and records which package may mint concept identifiers.

The owning package declares the active interchange and validation profile, including any documented relaxation of the one-preferred-label-per-language-tag constraint, before any concept record is published.

The owning package declares the language and script registries it validates against and the version or snapshot date of each, and reports registry unavailability rather than silently passing validation.
The owning package declares which neighbouring models master referents, subject fields and lexical entries, so that no referenced model's lifecycle is reproduced locally.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Concept IRIs are minted only in a namespace controlled by a named authority; local IDs in this model use lower-kebab-case and carry no date-like component. Designation identifiers are namespaced under the concept's owning package, never under a language tag, so a designation can change language metadata without changing identity. Notations are namespaced by their coding scheme and are never used as concept identifiers.
registry_links: IANA Language Subtag Registry for BCP 47 subtag validity, deprecation and Suppress-Script (SRC-009)
ISO 15924 script code registry maintained by the Unicode Consortium Registration Authority (SRC-010)
Published ISO 25964 to SKOS correspondence and the iso-thes namespace for thesaurus-profile mapping (SRC-007, SRC-008)
Publicly available TBX dialect specifications and validation schemas for terminological interchange (SRC-012)

canonicalization_rules: The canonical form of a concept record is the format-neutral set of identifiers, codes and language-tagged literals; RDF, TBX, JSON, YAML, Markdown and document-store representations are projections and are never authoritative.
Language tags are canonicalised to the case conventions of BCP 47 (lowercase language, titlecase script, uppercase region) and a script subtag is dropped when Suppress-Script applies to the language.

Literal forms are compared after a declared Unicode normalisation form; the chosen form is stated by the adopting Dimension and recorded with the record, because comparison results differ between forms.
patch_rules: A patch identifies its target by concept identifier and, for designation-level change, by designation identifier; targeting by literal string is rejected because strings are neither unique nor stable.

Changing a preferred designation, a definition or a subject field is a semantic patch and must state whether it is identity-preserving under the recorded identity rule; if it is identity-breaking, a split or merge is required instead of a patch.
A patch that would create a second preferred designation for one language tag is rejected unless the active profile documents the relaxation and the patch cites it.
compatibility_rules: Adding a designation, note or language is backward compatible; removing or re-rating a preferred designation is a breaking change for consumers that resolve by label.
A projection that cannot carry designation-level attributes must emit a loss report; publishing such a projection without the loss report is treated as a compatibility defect.
Conformance to SKOS, ISO 25964, TBX or OntoLex is asserted only per validated profile with attached evidence; alignment without validation is recorded as alignment, not conformance.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier assigned by the system of record for the concept or designation, such as a terminology-management entry identifier or a standards body's concept number.
Governed global identifier or IRI minted in a namespace controlled by a named authority, used when no master-system identifier exists or when a linked-data identity is additionally required.
UUID or ULID minted by the adopting Dimension, used only when neither of the above is available, and never derived from a label, notation, definition text or date.
A preferred label, a notation, a definition string and a date are never identifiers; a notation is unique only within its coding scheme and a label only within one language tag.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All time values are recorded as RFC 3339 date-time strings with explicit seconds and an explicit numeric offset or Z; -00:00 is used only for a known UTC instant whose local offset is unknown. Where they differ, the event time (when a designation was first attested, rated or discouraged) is recorded separately from the observation or ingestion time at which this model captured it, and neither time value is ever used as an identifier or as part of one.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts, currently the usage attestation series, are named as the owning designation identifier followed by a zero-padded, monotonically increasing sequence number assigned by the owning package. Sequence numbers are never reused after an attestation is withdrawn and never encode a date or a language tag.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every artifact records a named hash algorithm, its digest and a byte length. An artifact whose stored bytes do not match the recorded digest is treated as unresolvable: the referencing finding is marked unverified and the artifact is never silently repaired or re-hashed in place.

policies: Identity is carried by the concept, never by a label: no process may resolve, deduplicate or merge concepts on preferred-label equality alone.
No designation is coined to fill a language gap; a missing equivalent is recorded with an explicit no-equivalent marker and, where useful, a descriptive gloss marked as not being a term.

Alignment to an external standard is recorded as alignment; conformance is asserted only with attached validation evidence for a named profile, and known conflicts are recorded rather than resolved by assumption.

Runtime enforcement, approval workflow and audit-trail storage are not performed by this model; it holds policy and audit-record references and defers execution to the adopting Dimension and to the governance area of the combined model.

read: Concept identity, preferred and admitted designations, definitions and meaning-bearing notes are readable by any consumer authorised for the concept scheme.
Reads must state a language tag or a declared fallback order; a read that matches nothing returns an explicit no-designation signal rather than an arbitrary language.
Hidden designations are matchable in retrieval but are not returned for display unless the caller is explicitly permitted.
create: A concept record is created only with a primary identifier from the priority order and at least one delimiting characteristic.
A designation is created only with a validated language tag, a designation type and an acceptability rating.
Creation asserts no scheme membership, editorial status or approval; those are set by the scheme and lifecycle areas.
update: Updates target identifiers, never literal strings, and state whether the change is identity-preserving under the recorded identity rule.
Re-rating a designation updates the designation record and re-evaluates the preferred-label uniqueness constraint before the change is accepted.
An identity-breaking change is refused as an update and routed to a split or merge handled by the lifecycle area.
delete: Concept records are not hard-deleted by this model: a withdrawn concept identifier is retained as a tombstone carrying the identifier, a withdrawal-reason reference and any redirect target, so existing citations continue to resolve.
A designation removed from active use is retained with a status change on the designation record; only demonstrable data-entry errors are physically removed, and the removal is itself recorded.

Retention periods, legal hold, erasure requests and physical destruction are not executed here. Execution is owned by the adopting Dimension's retention and data-protection policy and, where a governance model is composed, by that model; this model carries only the policy reference and the tombstone.

Attestation artifacts containing third-party or personal content are withdrawn through the adopting Dimension's process; this model then retains the citation metadata and the tombstone but not the captured content.

roles.name: Concept owner
responsibilities: Approves concept creation, delimitation and split or merge decisions
Maintains the identity rule that separates identity-preserving from identity-breaking change

roles.name: Terminologist for a language
responsibilities: Maintains designations, ratings and lexical description for one language
Records usage context, discouraged usage and attestations
Records no-equivalent markers instead of coining terms

roles.name: Subject-matter authority
responsibilities: Supplies and validates definitions and delimiting characteristics
Confirms subject-field assignment and homograph disambiguation

roles.name: Interoperability steward
responsibilities: Maintains mappings to SKOS, ISO 25964, TBX, OntoLex and MVF profiles
Reviews loss reports and blocks unsupported conformance claims
Tracks language and script registry versions used in validation

roles.name: Validation operator
responsibilities: Runs constraint validation and publishes findings without remediating them
Reports registry unavailability rather than treating unchecked constraints as passed
Marks records unverified when artifact digests do not match

access.default_rule: Concept identity, preferred and admitted designations, definitions and meaning-bearing notes intended for publication are readable by any consumer authorised for the containing concept scheme; write access is limited to the concept owner and the terminologist for the affected language. Access decisions are evaluated and enforced by the adopting Dimension's access service, which this model references but does not implement.
exceptions: Hidden designations, including known misspellings and offensive variants, are matchable in retrieval but suppressed from display for all but explicitly permitted callers.
Concepts embargoed before publication of a standard or a product release are restricted to the owning package until the embargo reference clears.
Attestation artifacts reproducing third-party copyrighted text are restricted to callers covered by the applicable licence; unlicensed callers receive citation metadata only.
Appellations and proper names identifying living persons are subject to the adopting Dimension's data-protection restriction; this model flags the sensitivity and defers the decision.
audit_requirements: Every change to a concept identifier, a preferred designation, a definition or a subject-field assignment is recorded by the adopting Dimension's audit service with actor, RFC 3339 event time with offset, and before and after values.
This model stores only the audit record reference; audit storage, retention, evaluation and tamper-evidence remain owned by the audit service and the governance area of the combined model.
Validation findings and loss reports are retained with the record long enough to explain any published conformance or alignment claim.

read_order: AGENTS.md — resolve Name, Type and the four URLs before touching any record
Specification URL — the format-neutral semantics of concept, designation, definition and usage, including identity priority and the exclusive artifact rule
Storage type URL — how the canonical record is projected into the chosen store, including which registry snapshots are pinned
Interface URL — how to read, create and validate records, including the language fallback contract and the no-designation signal
Processes URL — who may rate designations, who owns split and merge decisions, and where enforcement, approval and audit are executed outside this model

coverage.claim: This is a standards-grounded semantic core for WM-KNW-006: concept identity and delimitation, designations with acceptability ratings and their own identity, language and script tagging, lexical form, definitions and typed notes, subject field, referents and usage, plus multilingual equivalence at the designation and sense boundary. It is sufficient for an agent to establish, inspect, resolve, validate and project a concept record independently of storage format. It deliberately excludes the scheme, semantic-relation, mapping, lifecycle, provenance, ownership, access and quality areas, which belong to the other areas of the combined model and are named in the boundary notes.

checklist.notes: Identifier priority ordered from authoritative master system through governed IRI to locally minted UUID or ULID; notation and preferred label explicitly excluded as identifiers; designation-level identity handled separately (SRC-001, SRC-002, SRC-008).

Concept and designation status, supersession, deprecation and versioning belong to the lifecycle area of the combined model. Only the identity-breaking trigger that forces a split or merge is retained here, and the update rule routes such changes out.

Covered narrowly and deliberately: denotation to referents, relations between designations, and cross-language equivalence. Hierarchical, associative and instantial concept relations and cross-scheme mappings are excluded and cited in boundary notes (SRC-004, SRC-008).

RFC 3339 with seconds and explicit offset is mandated, with event time separated from observation or ingestion time; attestation event time is a declared data element (SRC-011). Temporal versioning of the concept itself is not modelled here.

Covered narrowly at value level: definition source reference, transliteration scheme, attestation source and evidence for equivalence and delimitation. The full change and derivation chain is owned by the provenance area (SRC-005, SRC-009, SRC-012).

Concept ownership, editorial authority and stewardship assignment belong to the governance area. The semantic core carries only a reference-only rating-authority pointer on a designation; service_layers.roles describes operating roles, not owned governance semantics.

Preferred-label uniqueness per language tag and pairwise label disjointness, exactly one literal form per reified label, script subtag suppression, definition circularity check and interchange loss reporting; the validation function returns findings and performs no enforcement (SRC-001, SRC-002, SRC-009).

Access evaluation and enforcement are owned by the adopting Dimension's access service. service_layers.access states the default rule, four scopes and four exceptions as references; hidden designations are a display-suppression feature, not an access-control mechanism.

No retention semantics are owned here. service_layers.crud.delete states the tombstone rule for withdrawn concept identifiers and designations and names the adopting Dimension's retention and data-protection policy, with the governance area, as the owner of execution.

Alignments to SKOS and SKOS-XL, ISO 25964 iso-thes, TBX, OntoLex and MVF, with a mandatory loss report and a rule that conformance is claimed only with validation evidence (SRC-001, SRC-004, SRC-008, SRC-012).
Concept kind (general versus individual), designation type, definition type, note type, audience and register, and referenced subject-field values (SRC-005, SRC-006).
BCP 47 subtag order, IANA registry validation including Suppress-Script, ISO 15924 script codes, transliteration provenance and a declared language fallback contract (SRC-009, SRC-010).
The semantic core carries no quantitative measures. Quality scores, coverage metrics and inter-annotator agreement belong to the quality area of the combined model.

Appellations and proper names may identify living persons, and attestation artifacts may capture personal data. The model flags the sensitivity and defers handling, but no primary source consulted here settles whether a designation record constitutes personal data in a given jurisdiction.
Territory of currency for a designation via region subtags and named usage communities; no geometry or coordinate modelling is in scope (SRC-009).

known_omissions: Clause text of ISO 1087:2019, ISO 704, ISO 12620-1:2022, ISO 30042:2019 and ISO 24613 (LMF) is paywalled and was not read. ISO 1087 notions are grounded through the publicly retrievable OMG rendering (SRC-005) and no ISO clause is quoted.

The DatCatInfo data category repository was unreachable during research (connection refused), so no data-category persistent identifiers for part of speech, term type or administrative status are cited; grammatical category values are declared as registry-referenced without naming specific identifiers.

Sign-language designations, tactile designations and other non-written, non-audio modalities are only partially covered by the designation type and symbol artifact; no primary source consulted specifies their representation.

Concept scheme membership, hierarchical and associative relations, cross-scheme mapping, lifecycle, the full provenance chain, ownership, access and quality are not modelled here by instruction; they are in scope for the combined WM-KNW-006 and are cited in boundary notes.
No treatment of derived representations such as embeddings, ranked synonym expansion or automatically induced senses.
Unicode normalisation form is required to be declared but is not prescribed; comparison results for designations differ between NFC and NFD and no source consulted mandates one.
conflicts: SKOS condition S14 permits at most one skos:prefLabel per language tag, while terminology practice grounded in ISO 1087 and TBX allows several admitted terms and, in some termbases, more than one term rated preferred per language for different registers. A profile decision is required and is recorded rather than resolved.

Plain SKOS labels and reified designations (SKOS-XL, iso-thes preferred and non-preferred term classes, TBX term sections) are not interchangeable: projecting a reified designation to a plain literal silently drops rating history, source and grammatical data, which is why a loss report is mandatory.

OntoLex defines LexicalConcept as a subclass of skos:Concept, which invites treating a lexicalised concept as a terminological concept; ISO 1087 keeps concept and designation strictly apart. The model records the assertion level of any equivalence claim to keep the two apart.

The SKOS Primer states that OWL DL users cannot treat SKOS concepts as classes, yet many domain vocabularies do exactly that through punning. Any ontology projection must declare the OWL flavour assumed, and conformance claims that do not are rejected.

BCP 47 Suppress-Script guidance conflicts with the common practice of always emitting a script subtag; tags carrying a suppressed script do not match consumer expectations and are treated as a validation finding, not silently normalised.

The iso-thes namespace documentation lists custom term, concept and note attributes as unmodelled, so extension attributes carried in ISO 25964 XML have no agreed RDF form; such attributes are reported as loss rather than mapped by guesswork.
regional_assumptions: Language, script and region values assume the IANA Language Subtag Registry and the ISO 15924 registry are available and that the adopting Dimension pins a snapshot version; jurisdictions with national terminology or language authorities may impose a preferred-term authority that overrides scheme defaults.
Bilingual and multilingual jurisdictions may make a preferred designation in more than one official language mandatory; this model records the requirement as a reference and does not enforce it.
Data-protection regimes differ on whether appellations and proper names identifying living persons are personal data; treated as an open gap rather than assumed either way.
Right-to-left and non-Latin scripts assume the adopting Dimension declares a Unicode normalisation form and a collation for sorting designations; neither is prescribed here.
Subject-field classifications are frequently national or sectoral; the model references the classification and its version rather than assuming a single global scheme.
adversarial_checks: Attempted to justify a concept status and versioning layer because iso-thes defines a status property applying to concepts or labels; rejected, because concept status and versioning belong to the lifecycle area. Only designation usage status was retained, with an explicit constraint question preventing propagation between the two.

Attempted to model broader, narrower and related-concept relations, since SKOS defines them directly on skos:Concept and iso-thes refines them; rejected and moved to boundary notes and the relations area, so the semantic core owns no hierarchy.

Tested whether a preferred label could serve as the identifier; rejected because SKOS permits one preferred label per language tag, labels are language-scoped and mutable, and the same string recurs across schemes and subject fields. The policy layer now forbids resolving or merging on label equality.

Searched for a counterexample to the concept and designation split: non-linguistic symbols and appellations are designations with no lexical entry, which is why lexical form is attached at the designation boundary rather than at the concept, and why the designation-type code is mandatory.

Checked whether multilingual equivalence smuggles in cross-scheme mapping ownership; it does not — equivalence here holds between designations of a single concept, and concept-to-concept mapping is excluded in scope and boundary notes.

Audited every function against the no-enforcement rule: the validation function returns findings and explicitly disclaims remediation, enforcement and audit-record writing, and the resolve function is declared read-only with a no-designation signal instead of a coined fallback.
Verified that no artifact carries identity for a concept, that the only serial artifact has a sequence rule with no date component, and that no local ID contains a date-like element.

Checked each finding against the exclusive artifact rule: four findings declare artifacts with a null rationale and nine declare an empty artifact array with a substantive rationale; none populates both.
